pairs.question: Quid vos perdiderit, dicam?
pairs.derivation: The author poses the self-question 'Shall I tell what destroyed you?' (the speech-introducing dicam? is part of the rhetorical question) and answers it himself: you did not know how to love; you lacked the art. The answer stops before the general maxim 'arte perennat amor' that closes the couplet, which turns from answering to a sententia. First word capitalized, terminal full stop supplied at the cut.

pairs.question: Quid sapiens faciet, stultus cum munere gaudet?
pairs.answer: Ipse quoque accepto munere mutus erit.
pairs.derivation: The author asks what the wise (incorruptible) guardian will do, given that even the fool delights in a gift, and answers in the next line: he too, once a gift is accepted, will be silent. Clean one-sentence question and one-sentence answer; the answer ends at the line-final full stop, after which 'Sed semel est custos...' begins a new thought.
